Command: Swear by God's name when an oath is required
Summary: Deuteronomy 6:13 permits swearing by God's name when an oath is required: 'and shalt swear by his name.' Oaths were not to be sworn by other gods, binding the swearer's word to the LORD alone.
Commandment: When an oath is required, swear by God's name alone.
Application: The oath's weight comes from the name sworn by; swearing by other gods would bind the word to idols. The command guards truth-telling by anchoring oaths in the LORD.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: fear belongs with serving and cleaving to the God who brought Israel out of Egypt and keeps covenant (Deuteronomy 10:20-22).
